scope: Preliminary AI-assisted linguistic spot-check, not a human gold-standard accuracy estimate
reviewer: AI assistant linguistic spot-check; not independently adjudicated human gold annotation
limitations: Six four-year-old real children; one synthetic prompt pair, one generator and two reversed assignments.
Judgments were made by an AI assistant seeing the text and predicted annotations, without independent human adjudication.
No exhaustive word-level or attachment gold labels; no sensitivity/specificity, agreement coefficient, confidence interval or accuracy percentage is established.
Utterances are clustered and can repeat across stories/conditions; the audit is not an independent-sample experiment.
Ambiguous or malformed utterances can have more than one defensible analysis.
Real original boundaries are retained, while generated text uses predicted boundaries; segmentation effects cannot be separated from parsing quality in this comparison.
